topology.scratch_floor_trap: TRANSCODING_MIN_FREE_SCRATCH_MB=0 does NOT mean 'no floor': WithScratchGuard treats 0 as 'use DefaultMinFreeScratchBytes' (10 GiB), so on a 9 GiB-free machine every transcode job deferred with 'scratch space below the floor'. A small-disk lab must set a small POSITIVE value.
topology.kubo: 0.40.1, repos under the scratch dir with distinct IPFS_PATH and ports
topology.gateway_rig: IPFS_GATEWAY_URL points at a bare TCP pipe on :8082 forwarding to kubo's gateway on :8081. Killing the pipe leaves the node's RPC (:5011) answering 200 while every gateway URL is refused — the RPC-up/gateway-down split A31 measured and the follow-up's probe exists for. Killing the daemon would not reproduce it.
topology.irreversibility: Nothing was published. The public node ran --offline (Swarm not listening) with Routing.Type=none and no bootstrap peers; the private node ran under LIBP2P_FORCE_PNET=1 with a lab-generated swarm.key that is not committed. Every CID recorded here exists only on this machine.

stray_count_invisibility.mechanism: Service.strays is a per-process sync.Map, written by VerifyPins (runWorkers only, leader-gated) and read by probePublic via lastStrays. The api role serves /readyz and /admin/system and runs no workers, so its map is never written, Strays stays -1, and system_ipfs.go renders -1 as ABSENT by design.
stray_count_invisibility.positive_control: run as ONE process (api + workers), the first probe after a sweep rendered "unaccounted_node_pins": "2" — the two strays that existed (kubo's own welcome docs plus the file added by hand). The number is real and correct; it is unreachable from the surface on any deployment that separates the roles, which is what docker-compose.prod.yml renders.

SC4_block_lifecycle.block: POST /admin/videos/{id}/block flipped all 5 rows to 'unpinning' within 6s through the hook; the worker completed all 5 unpins; audit row {"ipfs_unpinned": "5"}

This is docs/operations.md's 'unpin != erasure, run repo gc' warning holding as written — a takedown does not complete on the instance's own gateway until the node's collector runs.

SC4_block_lifecycle.root_cause: SyncVideoCounted skips a terminal 'unpinned' row so a superseded generation's key is never resurrected. The HLS tree fell under that rule by accident: its key is stable across re-transcodes, it is deliberately absent from videoMirrorRefs (a directory intent, not a video_files row), and the only other path that arms it is OnTranscodeComplete. The four single-file classes came back because routePin re-claims them in any state.
SC4_block_lifecycle.fix: one narrow exception — the video's CURRENT HLS directory-intent key only, force re-claimed the way OnTranscodeComplete arms it, and only when the ledger already carries that row. TestSyncVideoRearmsTheHLSTreeAfterAnUnblock watched to fail first; TestSyncVideoLeavesASupersededTranscodeRowTerminal pins the negative.
SC4_block_lifecycle.quarantine_and_reject: entering quarantine needs no hook (the sweep converges, all 5 unpinned); approval re-pins all 5 through the real publish transition; POST /admin/videos/{id}/reject calls the seam explicitly — all 5 'unpinning' within 8s
